name: Shelter
label: Revelation
lede: Youth of Today's singer shaved his head, took vows, and brought a busload of monks on tour with a hardcore band, and for a few years in the '90s the pit was full of tulasi beads.

eras.title: The last Youth of Today record gets a new name
eras.text: Youth of Today was winding down and Ray Cappo had come back from India a Krishna devotee. He meant to make one final record about what he now believed, a farewell to punk's material world. Revelation Records heard it and decided it was a new band.

years.cap: The debut, released on Revelation the same year as Youth of Today's last album
years.h: Perfection of Desire: Ray Cappo's farewell becomes Shelter
years.p: Ray Cappo's goodbye-to-punk record comes out on Revelation under the name Shelter, the shelter a devotee takes in a guru and, finally, in Krishna. The credits list the players by first name only.
years.xp:
The idea was vegetarianism and straight edge followed to their end point: a spiritual life. Cappo wrote the songs as a statement of faith, and Revelation made the call to put them out as a new band rather than a Cappo solo record.

[[Sammy Siegler|869c662b-574c-46ac-acf6-3dc6f025fd5a]], who had joined Youth of Today at 15, says he drummed two songs on that first release.

years.h: Live at Bunratty's, Boston, 1990

eras.title: Monks in the van
eras.text: Shelter became a traveling temple. The lineup changed constantly, some players were celibate devotees and some were hardcore kids who liked the music, and the shows mixed chanting, vegetarian food and a pit. Hardcore gave it a name, sometimes as a sneer: Krishnacore.

years.h: Shelter's In Defense of Reality
years.p: Shelter's second record keeps the Krishna message front and center. Ray Cappo remakes its title track on the 2006 Shelter album Eternal.

years.h: Chris Interrante joins Shelter on bass
years.p: Chris Interrante plays bass in Shelter until 1993, and comes back for the 2018 reunion line-up.

years.h: Shelter's Quest for Certainty: two line-ups on one record
years.p: Revelation's credits split it: tracks 1 to 4 are [[Vic DiCara|a6698e1f-db17-4e93-9c4f-56678238e91f]], Chris Interrante and Eric Dailey; tracks 5 and 6 are [[Porcell|dff848b4-bb79-445a-81e1-3db65b7ddd3e]], Graham Land, a bassist credited as Yashomatinandana and a drummer listed as Sam.

years.h: Ray Cappo sells Equal Vision, the label he started for Shelter
years.p: Ray Cappo founded Equal Vision Records in Albany in 1990 to get Shelter and other Krishna releases out. In 1992 he sells it to label manager Steve Reddy, and the mission widens.
years.xp: Within a few years Equal Vision was putting out [[Converge|fa31e7d4-a03a-4110-98fc-f8826e95ec25]], Bane and [[Saves the Day|593f8594-83ad-4df4-a9b8-e4d225f55440]].

q: Dudes in Krishna robes playing hardcore. It was punk, dangerous, and badass.
years.h: Shelter's caravan tour with Inside Out and Quicksand
years.p: Sammy Siegler, 17, books Shelter a tour with [[Inside Out|0049c4d7-6459-4b54-a865-fd19969f427f]] and [[Quicksand|3c9f8bef-a658-4204-9ee8-7e95d2535b32]] off a phone list. Devotees ride in a school bus, and [[Zack de la Rocha|aa659468-db56-41c9-b6fe-61f4bb2ef1a6]] and the other non-devotees in a van.
years.xp:
The guru the band called the Maharaja traveled in a Winnebago.

Siegler remembers a fluorescent orange hat called the Conch: whoever held it got to talk. It was the only way to keep order among that many people on one tour.

Inside Out's [[Vic DiCara|a6698e1f-db17-4e93-9c4f-56678238e91f]] would cross over too, playing guitar in Shelter and later forming [[108|7f0c252a-bd45-4fe0-b306-478eeb07b97b]].

years.h: Shelter's Attaining the Supreme
years.p: The title of Shelter's 1993 album says it plainly. The band also puts out devotional side releases that year, Shelter Bhajan and Standard Temple Songs.

years.h: [[Porcell|dff848b4-bb79-445a-81e1-3db65b7ddd3e]] locks in on guitar in Shelter
years.p: Porcell, Ray Cappo's [[Youth of Today|9ca27db4-f127-4aeb-ae87-29e21f558c13]] partner, becomes Shelter's long-serving guitarist and, soon, its co-producer. He stays through 2000.

years.h: Norman Arenas joins Shelter on second guitar
years.p: Norman Arenas joins for the Attaining the Supreme tour while editing the zine Anti-Matter. AllMusic says he later formed [[Texas Is the Reason|b93c736f-a82f-4cae-9e57-a60b12d7055f]], briefly rejoined Shelter, and ended up in New End Original.

eras.title: A metal label signs the robes
eras.text: The mid-'90s put Shelter among the biggest hardcore bands going, next to Snapcase, Strife, Earth Crisis and Sick of It All. Roadrunner, home of Type O Negative, signed them, and the band landed on festival stages with Slayer, Venom and the reformed Sex Pistols. It was as close to crossover as Krishnacore ever got.

q: The article was all about how Krishnas brainwashed you.
years.h: Spin asks if Shelter's Krishna robes are a con
years.p: A Spin feature on Krishna hardcore lays out the case against it: Maximum Rocknroll had already run a scathing attack, and the writer notes the Krishna gurus preach an authoritarian worldview a long way from anarchy.
years.xp:
Norman Arenas, then Shelter's guitarist, remembered the MRR piece as a brainwashing story. The sharpest words came from inside the movement: former [[Cro-Mags|9ffa627f-32c2-4cb1-bfad-00cf348abc70]] singer [[John Joseph|64581915-b050-4a79-b1bf-29fdf6005093]] pointed to ISKCON's sex scandals and thievery and to Monkey on a Stick, a book on the Krishnas' drugs, guns and murders.

Joseph told Spin his own spiritual master had sex with a 15-year-old girl. The piece carried no response from Ray Cappo to the cult charge.

years.h: Shelter's Mantra · Roadrunner and Supersoul
years.p: Shelter's Roadrunner debut: eleven songs in about thirty minutes, produced by Tom Soares and Porcell. The booklet carries a Ray Cappo manifesto called Supersoul, which becomes the name of his imprint.
years.xp:
[[Dave DiCenso|fba8fbad-b75b-409a-8e91-4ef7cbb17605]] plays drums on the record. Sammy Siegler helped write the material but isn't on it. The songs pair Krishna philosophy with a running critique of Western life, in titles like Civilized Man and Surrender to Your T.V.

Critics split along the obvious line. Trouser Press called Cappo a principled spokesman for transcendental thought set to a tough 4/4 beat. Germany's Ox-Fanzine, looking back, heard a tame rock album from another time.

years.h: Shelter tour with Type O Negative
years.p: Roadrunner labelmates Shelter and Type O Negative share a bill that Sammy Siegler says kind of worked. On the road, a devotee hosts them for dinner at a saffron-painted mansion.

years.h: Live at Lee's Palace, Toronto, October 27, 1995
yt: Live at Lee's Palace, Toronto, October 27, 1995

years.h: Shelter play Brazil for the first time
years.p: Shelter play Brazil for the first time. The Brazilian edition of Mantra adds two bonus tracks, one of them a cover of the Beatles' We Can Work It Out.

years.h: Shelter's Beyond Planet Earth
years.p: Shelter's second and last Roadrunner album. The band's tours now run across North America, Europe and South America.

years.h: Shelter's tour van goes off a Colorado cliff
years.p: On the Beyond Planet Earth tour, Shelter's driver falls asleep and the van goes off a cliff in Colorado. AllMusic says everyone survives, but some band members are seriously injured and take months to recover.

eras.title: Twenty summers, then quiet
eras.text: By the turn of the century the Krishna wave in hardcore had crested, and Shelter pulled back from full-time preaching. Two more albums on two more labels, one last run of shows, and then a hiatus nobody called a breakup.

years.h: Shelter's When 20 Summers Pass · Victory
years.p: Shelter move to Victory Records for their 2000 album. It's also the year Porcell's first run in the band ends.

years.h: Shelter's The Purpose, the Passion · Supersoul
years.p: Released on Ray Cappo's own Supersoul imprint. Shelter tour Europe and the eastern U.S., then go on extended hiatus.

eras.title: The door never quite closed
eras.text: Shelter came back in pieces: a European tour, a Cappo record under the band's name, a pair of one-off shows on two continents. Cappo had moved to California by then; he'd later settle in upstate New York as a yoga teacher.

years.h: Shelter reunite for a European tour
years.p: A reunion tour takes Shelter back to Europe, where their audience never really went away.

years.h: Shelter's Eternal · Good Life Recordings
years.p: Essentially a Ray Cappo solo album under the Shelter name: ten new songs plus a remake of In Defense of Reality. A European tour follows.

years.h: Shelter play a reunion show in Gothenburg, Sweden
years.p: The first of two Shelter reunion shows ten days apart, on either side of the Atlantic.

years.h: Shelter play a reunion show in Reading, Pennsylvania
years.p: Ten days after Gothenburg, Shelter's second 2011 reunion show is back home in the U.S.

eras.title: Punk to monk to the Dome
eras.text: The classic players regrouped, Cappo wrote it all down, and Mantra came back on vinyl at thirty. In 2026 it gets billed as the other half of a Youth of Today night.

years.h: Shelter's classic line-up returns
years.p: Ray Cappo, [[Porcell|dff848b4-bb79-445a-81e1-3db65b7ddd3e]], [[Sammy Siegler|869c662b-574c-46ac-acf6-3dc6f025fd5a]] and Chris Interrante play a U.S. tour and a European festival as Shelter. Siegler is back on drums twenty-eight years after he drummed on Perfection of Desire.

years.h: Ray Cappo's memoir, From Punk to Monk
years.p: Ray Raghunath Cappo's memoir comes out on Mandala Publishing, with a foreword by [[Moby|8970d868-0723-483b-a75b-51088913d3d4]].

years.h: Shelter's Mantra at thirty
years.p: An anniversary vinyl edition puts Shelter's 1995 Roadrunner album back in record stores.

years.h: Ray Cappo plays two nights at the Dome, London
years.p: Ray Cappo is billed to front both [[Youth of Today|9ca27db4-f127-4aeb-ae87-29e21f558c13]] and Shelter at the Dome in London, the band he started when Youth of Today ended.
